title: Pair baseline and candidate timings to expose run-order drift
applies_when: A small latency difference may be confounded by warmup, cache state, thermal drift, competing load or separate benchmark sessions.
lesson: Match workload, concurrency, precision and timing boundaries across arms. Warm each arm appropriately, then collect nearby baseline/candidate pairs with randomized or balanced order. Retain paired differences and variability. If the apparent gain cannot be distinguished from drift and noise, report it as inconclusive rather than choosing a favorable session.
avoid_when: Pairing does not repair unequal configurations or state leaking between arms. Use independently initialized processes when necessary and randomize their order. Cold-start objectives need their own comparable cold-start measurements.

evidence.note: Google Benchmark documents random interleaving to reduce system-state effects. Pairing and process isolation here are experimental-design suggestions, not proof of a measured improvement.
